import pytest


def strlen(string: str) -> int:
    return len(string)


# Unit test for function strlen
def test_strlen():
    # Basic cases
    assert strlen("") == 0
    assert strlen("a") == 1
    assert strlen("abc") == 3

    # Strings with spaces
    assert strlen("hello world") == 11
    assert strlen("   ") == 3

    # Special characters and unicode
    assert strlen("!@#$%^&*()") == 10
    assert strlen("héllo") == 5
    assert strlen("你好") == 2

    # Newlines and tabs
    assert strlen("line\n") == 5
    assert strlen("\t") == 1

    # Longer string
    assert strlen("a" * 1000) == 1000

# Unit test for function strlen
def test_strlen():
    # Empty string
    assert strlen("") == 0
    # Single character
    assert strlen("a") == 1
    # Typical strings
    assert strlen("abc") == 3
    assert strlen("hello") == 5
    # Spaces count as characters
    assert strlen("hello world") == 11
    assert strlen("   ") == 3
    # Special characters
    assert strlen("!@#$%") == 5
    # Unicode characters
    assert strlen("héllo") == 5
    assert strlen("日本語") == 3
    # Whitespace escape characters
    assert strlen("\n\t") == 2
    # Long string
    assert strlen("x" * 1000) == 1000
    # Return type is int
    assert isinstance(strlen("test"), int)
